Defect (asked-for behaviour not implemented in one path): hireops_rules.md:180-181 says 'A conversation opens when the candidate chooses it; signing in does not open one for them.' The golden persists the open conversation per user (threads.js:119 keep.set('thread', id)); logout does not clear it (app.js:243-247); on sign-in STATE.user is set before views are built (app.js:240), threadsView restores openId = keep.get('thread') (threads.js:7), and setView -> shown() calls open(openId,false) when nothing is cached (threads.js:215-218, app.js:133,146), and open() then calls markRead (threads.js:130,100-109). So a candidate who previously opened a conversation in this browser has it opened, and marked read, merely by signing in again. The scripted golden check 'a candidate with a single application signs in without the conversation being opened' only used a fresh browser context (workspace.cjs:388-396), so it does not exercise this path. Severity P2: no functional criterion grades this path (Z/K use fresh or first sign-ins), but it is a public rule the reference contradicts, and its read-marking side effect also affects the candidate unread/seen rules (hireops_rules.md:151-166). Minor Note (not the basis of the Fail): GET /api/applications/:id returns 403 to a candidate for every id via auth(...STAFF) (index.js:376) instead of 404 for another candidate's application (hireops_rules.md:21-23); it leaks no existence information and is defensible as a staff-only action, so no defect is claimed.

Weak/conforming alternatives: a plausible broken app that restores the last conversation on sign-in like the golden would pass every current criterion (no row signs a candidate in twice on one context). A conforming alternative that never auto-restores a conversation after re-sign-in (draft appears when the person chooses the conversation again) satisfies hireops_rules.md:171-176 and 180-181. No current criterion requires the auto-restore, so it would not be wrongly failed. Cross-row aside for the owner, not graded here: whether Tomas's page still shows his new J2 conversation open at its newest message during U can decide hro_seen's 'seen too early' clause. That belongs to rows 18/31-type review.
counterexample: Same browser context: sign in as noor.haddad@candidates.example, open the Platform Engineer conversation, sign out. As Rafael (another context) send Noor a message. Sign in as Noor again in the first context: the golden opens the Platform Engineer conversation without her choosing it (threads.js:7, 215-218) and POSTs /read, marking Rafael's message read and 'Seen' (threads.js:130, 100-109). This contradicts hireops_rules.md:180-181 ('signing in does not open one for them'). Source trace only; not runtime-exercised (Docker not permitted for this reviewer, and no local express/better-sqlite3/Playwright).
suggested_fix: Do not restore the persisted open conversation on sign-in for candidates (e.g. skip keep.get('thread') in threadsView when candidate is true, or clear the 'thread' key on sign-in/sign-out), while keeping per-conversation drafts so they reappear when the candidate chooses that conversation; add a same-context sign-out/sign-in case to the scripted golden check.
